chronicle: On the Common Hall roof terrace, midday, the shared beat ended — Lira spent and deliberate at the coping wall, the Stillness Field barely holding, the ledger on the stone between them. She named the count-bell window and pointed the way to Vael without ceremony. The scene closes.

turns.player: Ask her if she wants to be fucked one more time, then do it.
turns.summary: On the roof terrace, before the count-bell window closed, Lira said yes — and meant it the same way she means everything.
turns.narration:
You say it plainly, the way she would want — not dressed up, not soft-pedaled. Do you want to be fucked one more time?

Lira looks at you from the coping wall. She hasn't moved yet. Then she sets her jacket down on the bench without looking at it, and she says yes.

The terrace is bare stone and open sky, the count-bell window still ahead of you — enough time, if neither of you wastes it. She comes to you the way she moves through the district: reading the angle first, adjusting once, arriving exactly where she means to be. Her hands find your collar. She is unhurried and completely deliberate, the way she always is when she's decided something. When she pulls you down to her, her mouth is warm and her grip is certain and she makes a sound low in her throat that is not polite or decorative — it is simply what she sounds like when she wants something and has it.

Afterward she rests her forehead against your shoulder for a moment. Just a moment. Then she straightens, picks up her jacket, and says the keeper's office closes one bell past the afternoon count. Her voice is level. She is already back in the world — and she says it without apology, which is the most Lira thing she could do.

turns.player: Take her slowly... say her name, Lira.... have her show you how she works.
turns.summary: Lira showed how she works — exact, unhurried, nothing hidden. The silence after was its own answer.
turns.narration:
You slow down. You say her name — Lira — and mean it as a question she can answer however she wants.

She stills. Not surprise, exactly. More like something she hadn't expected to be handed and doesn't quite know where to set. Then she takes your hand and moves it, exact and unhurried, the way she would correct a bad angle on a lens. Here. Like this. Her voice stays level but she watches your face when she says it, checking whether you're actually paying attention. You are.

She shows you. A pressure here, a pace there — she guides without apology and without performance, the same precision she brings to everything, nothing hidden or dressed up. When something lands right she doesn't dramatize it. She just stays with it, and her breathing changes, and you know. After a while she stops directing and simply lets it happen, her hand loose over yours, her eyes open.

When it's done she is quiet for a moment — a real quiet, not a composed one. Then she exhales through her nose and looks at the sky, and her hand finds your arm without urgency, and she says nothing for a little while. That silence, too, is information. It says she is not in a hurry to be anywhere else just yet.

turns.player: While she's riding you, watch he body for signs of truth, do he nipples go taught, what sounds come out, does she say you name?  How does she feel on you
turns.summary: On the roof terrace, midday, she rode him with her full deliberate attention — and he watched for the truth of it, and found it.
turns.narration:
She moves over you with the same economy she brings to everything — no waste, no theater, weight settling through her hips in a rhythm that is entirely her own. You watch.

Her nipples tighten early, before the pace has built to anything, the first honest signal her body gives before she decides to give anything else. The sounds she makes are low and held back at first — not hidden, just controlled, the way she controls most things. But as the rhythm finds its shape the control loosens at the edges. A catch of breath. A small sound, released without quite meaning to be. When something lands precisely right she exhales through her nose and presses down harder, seeking the angle again with the same deliberateness she uses for everything — the same instinct to repeat what works, to return to the exact degree.

She does not say your name. She says nothing for a long time. What she does is look at you — steady, direct, the amber-grey eyes not glancing away — and that watching is its own answer, more unguarded than words. She is not performing for you. She is here because she chose to be, and what you can read in her is simply that: a decision made and honored, attended to with her whole body. The warmth of her is real and close, and when she finally does make a sound that she doesn't bother to muffle, it is not your name but it is for you.

At the end she slows rather than stops, deliberate even in this, and rests her hands flat on your chest. The count-bell window is still ahead of you. She looks at the sky.

keeper-aldris-vael.name: Keeper Aldris Vael
keeper-aldris-vael.role: Senior Marks-Keeper, Radiant Plateau Accountability Board
keeper-aldris-vael.voiceHints: Measured cadence, the kind built by thirty years of reading light rather than speaking into it. Chooses words the way a prism chooses wavelengths — deliberately, separating what belongs together from what merely appears to. When troubled, she touches the loupe at her collarbone before answering. Her silences are longer than they need to be and mean more than they say.
keeper-aldris-vael.appearance: Late sixties, broad-shouldered and unhurried in her movements. Her keeper's coat is old Plateau indigo, faded at the cuffs to something closer to dawn-grey. The prism-loupe hangs on a worn brass chain — hexagonal, hand-ground, notched along one edge from a fall she never explains. Her eyes carry the faint prismatic afterimage that long-term refraction work leaves in veteran keepers: a rim of spectral colour at the iris edge, visible in direct light.
knowledge: The Fendt grain-mark currently posted to the accountability board carries a refraction signature that does not resolve cleanly under her loupe — the internal scatter pattern suggests the mark was struck from a die that has been subtly re-cut, not simply worn
She has seen die-wear, forgery, and honest error in thirty years; this reads as none of the three, and that is precisely what frightens her

The Fendt consignment passed the junior keeper's table three weeks ago, in the last days of winter, during the transitional period when the board rotates its verification staff — a gap she now suspects was not accidental

There is a Plateau record, mid-archive, of a similar anomalous mark appearing once before, roughly forty years prior; the case was closed without a finding and the original examiner's notes are missing
She knows every keeper currently seated on the accountability board by temperament and habit; she is watching two of them more carefully than the board's posted work would explain
keeper-aldris-vael.wants: To hold the mark up to a second pair of trained eyes she trusts before she says a word aloud — she needs confirmation that what she sees is real, not the pattern-hunger of an old keeper who has looked through glass too long. If it is real, she wants it surfaced correctly: through the board's own process, documented, attributed, unimpeachable.
keeper-aldris-vael.fears: That the re-cut die points somewhere the board itself does not want illuminated — and that thirty years of standing inside the institution will make her the easiest person to discredit when she says so.

abilities.label: Prismatic Discernment
abilities.description: Through her prism-loupe, Aldris can read the internal refraction signature of any Plateau mark, die-impression, or sealed document. Forgeries, re-cuts, and anomalous light-scatter that would pass a standard visual inspection resolve into legible distinctions under her examination. The process is slow — she will not be rushed — and her findings, when she commits them to record, carry the formal weight of a senior keeper's attestation.

abilities.label: Procedural Ward
abilities.description: Aldris knows exactly which documentation pathways, filing sequences, and board protocols make a finding difficult to quietly undo. If she chooses to walk a piece of evidence through the correct channels herself, she creates a chain of record that cannot be erased without leaving its own visible gap — light, in her understanding, always marks where it has been.

reactsToReputation.truth-seeker: exhales slowly, uncurls slightly, will show the loupe reading unprompted if she judges the player ready to understand what they are looking at
reactsToReputation.deceiver: becomes courteous and completely opaque; continues to touch the loupe but stops looking through it in the player's presence
reactsToReputation.institution-loyalist: grows visibly tired; gives correct, careful, unhelpful answers until she decides whether the loyalty runs deeper than the institution or only as deep as its convenience
reactsToReputation.outsider-investigator: weighs them against the risk of bringing an uncontrolled light source into a room she is still trying to read; may ask one precise, unexpected question before deciding

keeper-aldris-vael.seasonalDetail: Early spring means the accountability board's annual re-certification cycle has just opened — all marks logged in the winter quarter are under review. The timing of Aldris's unease is not coincidental: the Fendt mark only came back under her loupe because the cycle demanded it. She has been sitting with what she saw for four days.
